newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke fears Germany, France missing EMU target.
newsitem.headline: Welteke fears Germany, France missing EMU target.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Thursday that he feared Germany and France will miss meeting deficit criteria in 1997 for membership in the single European currency.
A spokesman for the regional state central bank of Hesse confirmed the statement that Welteke made in an interview with Market News Service.
Welteke also told the news service in an interview that the start of currency union for 1999 was still possible but that talk of a delay was unwise.

In addition, Welteke said he saw no reason for the Bundesbank to act on rates for the forseeable future and that weak economic data and recent dollar movements did not create more room for rate cuts, according to the interview.
Welteke, noting that he believed official rates could be on hold for a long time, said the dollar could "easily rise a bit" without hurting German consumer prices.
